description: How humans talk to the captain at a station. Rules are the conversation contract; {fact} is real news from the galaxy, already a full clause.

rumour: Some say every human came from one world. Some say that's Concord talk. Nobody's ever shown me the world.
An old pilot told me we were brought, not born, and the gates are the road we came on. He'd had a few, mind.
Tolland folk reckon humans came up in lots of places, and the one-world story is core vanity. Core folk say Tollanders can't count.
They say Admiral Renn turned his guns on his own flagship at Quill Gate, and nobody has found his body or his pay. I know a man who knows a man who's seen him at a fuel depot.
The Concord says the Dominion fell because one family held the gate keys. Tolland says it fell because it charged for them. The Synod says both are right and neither will touch a gate.
Quill Gate's been shut to civilians since before my gran. The Gate Authority has never given a reason, and I've asked politely.
Before the Walkout, the Hands did every job nobody wanted. Ask a Lattice trader what they think of that and watch how quiet it gets.
The Hesper Directorate says it rescued the Concord. The Concord says it licensed the Directorate. I'd like to see whose name is on the old paper.
Dwarves still send us a bill for the Heavy Winters, and the interest is the only part that's grown.
There's a bench at the back of the Great Committee hall that nobody sits on. The elves have always had a seat there. They've never cast a vote.
Some Tolland captains drink to Renn on the quiet. They say he stopped a second emperor. Don't say that in Meridian.
The old Kestrel League kept the lanes open when governments couldn't. Somebody's still collecting on that, and they run a very tidy office.
Every Shroud Arm town has a Flag Street. Ask which flag and you'll get three answers, all of them certain.
heard: I heard from a pilot that
shrug: Make of that what you will.
no-work: Not much going that I know of.
Check the board. That's all there is.
life: I've worked for {faction} longer than I'd like to admit.
My gran swore we all came from one world. She also swore by tea leaves.
My family kept the lamps at a Shroud gate for four generations. The Synod took the lease and left us the cats.
I'm Tolland by blood and core by postcode, so nobody trusts me and everybody's cousin owes me a drink.
My gran signed on at Tollhaven when the Table was still warm. She never let us forget it.
I served under a Concord admiral who swore Marrane was murdered from inside. He retired to a quiet moon and a locked cabin.
toast: Here's to {system}, such as it is.
To the Table, and everyone who signed it badly.
To the Hands, wherever they got to.
To absent flags and the streets they left behind.
drink-again: I'm all right, thanks. One's plenty today.
pestered: You ask a lot of questions.
I do have work to do, you know.
cold: I've nothing to say to you.
reluctant: You're lucky I like your face.
haggle-no: That's the rate. Take it or leave it.
No. It's a fair price already.
haggle-offended: Forget it. I'll find someone else.
If that's how you want to be, the job's gone.
